phase: F1 — Engineering Safety Net and Concurrency Verification
title: Emergency-contact primary-update race — root-cause confirmation and fix

priorF1004P1EvidenceFile.note: Only existed on unmerged/closed PR #311, which self-recorded supersession by PR #310.

rootCause.explanation: PR #310's optimistic-concurrency 'prior primary' snapshot was read via a separate, unlocked prisma.patientEmergencyContact.findFirst() call issued before prisma.$transaction() opened. That query and the transaction's own connection checkout compete independently for the same pg pool (server/src/db.ts, default max 10). Under contention, the losing request's prior-read could be delayed until after the winning request's entire transaction had already committed, causing the in-lock recheck to find no discrepancy.
rootCause.whyStressTestCouldPass: The failure is scheduling-sensitive: it requires the exact window between the decoupled pre-check read and the transaction's own connection checkout to straddle the competing request's full commit. Repeated back-to-back rounds on an otherwise-idle process do not reliably reproduce that specific contention pattern.

deterministicRepro.method: AsyncLocalStorage-tagged monkey-patch gate on prisma.patientEmergencyContact.findFirst, scoped to the exact prior-primary query shape (isPrimary:true, no id filter, select {id:true}), forcing request B's read to wait for request A's full commit while both were dispatched via Promise.all

resultAgainstFixedCode.note: decoupled query no longer exists in fixed code

alternativeRejected.regressionScenario: scenario 5 (two unrelated patients, different organizations) started returning 409 for patient Y's concurrent create
alternativeRejected.probeMethod: raw pg client, no Prisma, no app code — three scenarios: true-overlap (correctly aborted, SQLSTATE 40001), full-sequential-B-after-A-commit (not caught by SERIALIZABLE, formally valid serial history), full-sequential-separate-connections (same result)

fixSelected.lockPrimitive: pg_advisory_xact_lock, keyed by patientId, unchanged from PR #310
fixSelected.orderingRequirement: prior read MUST precede acquireEmergencyContactPrimaryLock; both on the same tx
fixSelected.errorMapping: isPrimaryContactConflict() now checks P2002 (unique-index backstop) OR PrimaryContactConflictError.code OR P2034 (defensive)
fixSelected.residualLimitation: A request whose ENTIRE database interaction (including its own first statement) happens to be scheduled strictly after a competing request's full commit cannot be distinguished from a legitimately sequential operation by any purely server-side mechanism without a client-supplied concurrency token (would change API semantics) or a global lock (forbidden). Documented, not glossed over.

rollback.postRollbackBehavior: PR #310's exact prior design restored — the specific decoupled-query race becomes probabilistically (not deterministically) reproducible again under real scheduling/CI contention, at the same rate that produced the original CI failure
